column1: Two Causes of Rising and Falling Inflation The second and third terms in the Phillips curve equation show the two forces that can change the rate of inflation. The second term, b(u – u n), shows that cyclical unemployment—the deviation of unemployment from its natural rate—exerts upward or downward pressure on inflation. Low unemployment pulls the inflation rate up. This is called demand-pull inflation because high aggregate demand is responsible for this type of inflation. High unemployment pulls the inflation rate down. The parameter b measures how responsive inflation is to cyclical unemployment.
